subject: Civil Engineering
title: Water-Cement Ratio: The Key to Strength
description: A 60-second lesson on Water-Cement Ratio: The Key to Strength.

hook.text: Add more water and concrete flows easily. But it becomes weaker — much weaker.

buildup.text: The water-cement ratio (w/c) is the mass of water divided by the mass of cement.

discovery.text: Lower w/c means less porosity, higher strength, and better durability — but harder to place.

twist.text: Workers often add water on-site for easier pouring — this violates the design and weakens it.

climax.text: High-performance concrete uses w/c ratios below 0.30 — superplasticizers provide flow.

punchline.text: Less water, stronger concrete. It's the simplest rule and the most violated.

quiz.question: Why does adding extra water to concrete on-site cause problems?
options: Water makes the concrete set too quickly to work with
Excess water increases porosity, reducing strength and durability
Water reacts with steel reinforcement and causes immediate rusting
